In [[probability theory]], '''Bobkov's inequality'''  is a [[functional (mathematics)|functional]] [[isoperimetric inequality]] for the canonical [[Gaussian measure]]. It generalizes the [[Gaussian isoperimetric inequality]].
The equation was proven in 1997 by the [[Russia|Russian]] mathematician [[Sergey Bobkov]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Sergey G.|last1= Bobkov|title=An isoperimetric inequality on the discrete cube, and an elementary proof of the isoperimetric inequality in Gauss space|volume=25|journal=The Annals of Probability|number=1|publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|pages=206–214|date=1997|doi=10.1214/aop/1024404285|s2cid= 120975922|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Bobkov's inequality ==
''' Notation: '''

Let
*<math>\gamma^n(dx)=(2\pi)^{-n/2}e^{-\|x\|^2/2}d^nx</math> be the canonical Gaussian measure on <math>\R^n</math> with respect to the [[Lebesgue measure]],
*<math>\phi(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}</math> be the one dimensional canonical Gaussian density
*<math>\Phi(t)=\gamma^1[-\infty,t]</math> the cumulative distribution function
*<math>I(t):=\phi(\Phi^{-1}(t))</math> be a function <math>I(t):[0,1]\to [0,1]</math> that vanishes at the end points <math>\lim\limits_{t\to 0} I(t)=\lim\limits_{t\to 1} I(t)=0.</math>

=== Statement ===
For every [[Lipschitz continuity|locally Lipschitz continuous]] (or [[smooth function|smooth]]) function <math>f:\R^n\to[0,1]</math> the following inequality holds<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Sergey G.|last1= Bobkov|title=An isoperimetric inequality on the discrete cube, and an elementary proof of the isoperimetric inequality in Gauss space|volume=25|journal=The Annals of Probability|number=1|publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|pages=209|date=1997|doi=10.1214/aop/1024404285|s2cid= 120975922|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|first1=Eric|last1=Carlen|first2=James|last2=Kerce|date=2001|page=2|title=On the case of equality in Bobkov's inequality and Gaussian rearrangement|volume=13|journal=Calculus of Variations|doi=10.1007/PL00009921|s2cid=119968388 }}</ref>

:<math>I\left( \int_{\R^n} f d\gamma^n(dx)\right)\leq \int_{\R^n} \sqrt{I(f)^2+|\nabla f|^2}d\gamma^n(dx).</math>

== Generalizations ==
There exists a generalization by [[Dominique Bakry]] and [[Michel Ledoux]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Dominique|last1=Bakry|first2=Michel|last2=Ledoux|date=1996|title=Lévy–Gromov's isoperimetric inequality for an infinite dimensional diffusion generator|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=123|issue=2 |pages=259–281|doi=10.1007/s002220050026|s2cid=120433074 }} </ref>
